Etymology

Etymology[]

His name is a pun on the animal "python," a species of a large snake. His middle name is unknown,[30] but it starts with "P." His last name consists of two words, the first is "chums" and the second is "worth".

Behind the scenes

Behind the scenes[]

  • In the promotional image from 2012, Pythor uses recolored pieces of Fangtom's torso and tail and has his mouth closed, which, however, does not show up on a real minifigure.
    • However, Legacy Pythor has a slightly similar design to Pythor in this image.
  • In the Tournament of Elements sets, Pythor is featured as an antagonist who sides with the Anacondrai Cultists and battles the ninja. His role in the TV show is completely different, as he is really entirely against the Cultists and eventually winds up siding with the ninja to defeat them. This was likely done to make his defection in the show a plot twist.
  • Pythor's role in the third season can be compared to that of Saruman the White from The Lord of the Rings book and film series, as both are villains in white robes who act as an enforcer to a Dark Lord, and just like Saruman saw Sauron as an equal, Pythor himself saw the Overlord as an equal. The Great Devourer's acid eventually turns Pythor white, further reinforcing this.
  • Pythor is similar to Randall Boggs from Monsters, Inc. Both are purple reptilian creatures with the ability to turn invisible. They also both have a thirst for power.
  • In particular, the reticulated python is the longest species of snake in the world (although not the biggest overall), just as Pythor is the tallest Serpentine and has the longest neck in the show (not counting Clouse's pet).
  • Pythor P. Chumsworth is the first Serpentine with known last name, being succeeded by SsssSsss Underwood and the Slitherbottoms; although it is only mentioned in "Never Trust a Snake," Pythor's Revenge, "Blue Lightning," and "Kryptarium Prison Blues".
    • It is never revealed what the "P" stands for, and no one knows, according to Tommy Andreasen.[30]
      • Michael Dobson, Pythor's voice actor, jokingly said that the "P" stands for "Proud."[31]
    • Creators had about a dozen alternate names for him lined up as Tommy Andreasen was sure the name "Pythor" wouldn't get legal clearance.[30]
  • Every Pythor's minifigure except his Tournament of Elements and the Legacy minifigure has some inconsistencies with his designs in the show.
    • While he had purple arms in the TV show, his original minifigure in 9449 Ultra Sonic Raider featured black arms.
    • His original minifigure has red eyes, although his eyes are pink in the TV show.
    • His Day of the Departed minifigure has white gloves instead of purple hands he had in the special.
    • His Crystalized minifigure has eyeliner that is absent in the show.
  • Pythor's appearance as the Stranger resembles Entity 303, a Minecraft creepypasta. Both of them wear white hoodies with the hood shadowing their faces, and have glowing red eyes.
  • There are several changes between Pythor's design in Rebooted and Tournament of Elements due to the release of the physical minifigure, namely slightly different purple symbols and the complete absence of yellow on his head and tail, with the symbols on the front of the lower body having a white hole in the center that was not there before.
  • He is one of twelve Serpentine to have their name mentioned in the original series, the others being Skales, Acidicus, Skales Jr., Arcturus, Clancee, Raggmunk, Blunck, Machia, Aspheera, Char and Mambo V.
  • His white robe as "the stranger" is based on Mace Windu's most commonly used torso design from LEGO Star Wars.
  • Pythor's appearance in "Blue Lightning" is different from his original appearance. In addition to his Legacy appearance, he no longer has scales and has smaller red eyes without an eyeliner instead of larger pink ones, and the hip section that he had prior to Season 4 is gone.
    • His tail is also almost completely static and has the same shape as a physical LEGO piece. This is probably done to save money on the animation in the shorts, as he and the other Serpentine have no scales at all.
  • Pythor, along with Chen, is Tommy Andreasen's favorite villain because he's funny.[32]
  • When asked if Pythor will return, Tommy Andreasen said, "If an opportunity ever presents itself. These things need to happen organically though."[33]
    • His return in Season 15: Crystalized was confirmed in 2022, 1 year after the asking while most likely Pythor's return was already known among the creators.
  • According to Tommy Andreasen, the reason Pythor was bleached in Rebooted is that "the designers wanted a new look for him. We've explained it with stomach acids."[34]
  • Of the five original Serpentine general minifigures, Pythor is the only one with a rotatable head. This is because his head mold does not extend over the back of the torso like the others.
  • He has a very different appearance from the rest of his tribe, as he has a much longer neck, has a slightly more purple scales without a hint of pink, and has pink eyes instead of red ones and marking patterns on his tail. According to Tommy Andreasen, there is "no canon explanation" for this and it "just new production."[35]
    • However, his eyes were red in the flashback in "Spellbound," where it was caused by being hypnotized. He also has red eyes after soaking in the Devourer's stomach acids.
  • Unlike the other Serpentine, Pythor has three-dimensional scales in the WildBrain animation as in the WILFilm animation, unlike the two-dimensional scales used on the other WildBrain animated Serpentine characters.
    • In the music video of the 15th anniversary Weekend Whip, which was animated using Unreal Engine 5, Pythor has two-dimensional scales again.
  • Pythor's design in Season 15 is inspired by his original appearance and his Legacy design used in Tales from the Monastery of Spinjitzu. While retaining his three-dimensional scales and white color, his head and face design is the same as in "Blue Lightning," with no purple eye border and purple markings not appearing on his tail at all.
  • Pythor, Skales, and Acidicus are the only Serpentine generals to appear in the WildBrain seasons.
    • However, unlike Skales and Acidicus, Pythor has a new design, probably because he plays a more prominent role in the season than the previous two in seasons 11 and 14.
  • Pythor's neck has been significantly shortened over the years, although its length always varies depending on the scene.[36][37]
  • Pythor's ability to smell with his tongue shown in "Safe Haven" is the real ability of real-life snakes who smell with their forked tongues.
Trivia

Trivia[]

  • Pythor, the rest of the Anacondrai, Clancee and Frak are the only Serpentine who don't put extra emphasis on "S" sounds when they are talking.
  • Pythor appeared in every episode of the first season from his debut to his assumed death, for a total of ten appearances.
    • Due to his return in Rebooted, Pythor has become the Serpentine character with the most appearances in the show.
  • Pythor is one of the longest-running villains in the series, serving as the main antagonist of Season 1, the secondary antagonist of Season 3, a supporting character in Season 4, one of the secondary antagonists of "Day of the Departed," and a major antagonist of Season 15.
    • Because of this Pythor is likely the ninja's oldest enemy.
  • The Character Encyclopedia states that he was general of the Anacondrai, but now he's the tribe's last surviving member. However, Pythor was not a general.
    • Furthermore, it was later revealed that Strike, another Anacondrai member, survived as well.
  • Pythor is the only named character in the show known to be a cannibal, due to the fact that he ate his own kind while locked in the Serpentine tomb.
    • According to Tommy Andreasen, it is also possible that he ate his own mother.[38]
    • It was stated on LEGO.com that "a quick look through his things revealed recipes for Snake Soufflé, Anacondrai Au Vin, Cobra Cobbler, Roast Reptile and Serpentine Surprise."[25]
  • Pythor is the first character who speaks with a British accent. The second is Killow and the third is Kalmaar.
  • Pythor is similar to Nadakhan in several respects.
    • Both are charming, charismatic leaders who are the perceived "last of their kind."
      • It was later revealed that at least one other Djinn and one other Anacondrai are still alive.
    • Both stood out from the rest of their species, with Pythor having a different appearance from the other Anacondrai despite not being a general and Nadakhan being selfish, greedy, and disrespectful in a race of otherwise honorable djinns.
    • Both ultimately lost support and friendship from their underlings.
    • Both were imprisoned by their enemies long before the series began, only to be freed in their debut episode, going on to become the main antagonists of their season.
    • Finally, both suffered defeat in an ironic fashion: Pythor was eaten by the Great Devourer after awakening it, while Nadakhan was forced to undo the events of Skybound by Jay's final wish.
  • He is also similar to Kalmaar in several respects.
    • Both are purple non-human villains without legs and with a new head mould designed just for them.
    • Both first appear in the fourth episode of the season where they serve as the main antagonist.
    • Both speak with a British accent.
    • Both committed murder of at least three members of their own kind.
    • Both have eyes of a different color on the physical minifigure than in the show.
    • They both wish to awaken a giant serpent: Wojira and the Great Devourer respectively.
      • Coincidentally, both were devoured by the ones who they wished to re-awaken. However, while Pythor survived albeit with his completely bleached scales, Kalmaar was killed completely.
      • However, Pythor awakened the Great Devourer in the penultimate episode, whereas Kalmaar awakened Wojira earlier.
  • Pythor almost always appears in large sets: 9449 Ultra Sonic Raider, 70750 Ninja DB X, 70596 Samurai X Cave Chaos, 70679 The Ultra Dragon, and 71775 Nya's Samurai X MECH. The only exception is 70668 Jay's Storm Fighter.
  • According to Tommy Andreasen, Pythor was most likely a coward during the Serpentine War[39] and a "low ranking opportunist."[4] It is also possible that due to his long neck (possibly due to a mutation or birth defects) made him an outcast from the rest of his tribe.[40]
  • In addition to his long neck, Pythor shares some similarities with the Anacondrai serpent when compared to the rest of the Anacondrai. Both have pink eyes, a darker purple color, and shorter snouts.
  • The blue gem on Pythor's chest may hint that the Serpentine came from Chima.[41]
  • While the Anacondrai do not exist in the non-canon series containing Kingdom of the Snakes, Pythor's name is mentioned by Lasha in the book.
  • Though Pythor does not know Spinjitzu, he seems to be doing it on the Ninjago Spinners card "Swap You."
  • Pythor's name can be seen in the credits for the episode "Blackout," despite his appearance in the episode was as the "Mysterious Stranger" and intended to be a surprise.
    • However, the episode and the following episode aired back to back, so this detail was not notable.
  • Although Pythor was responsible for releasing the Great Devourer, most civilians never found out, as they saw only the large serpent destroying the city and did not know what had happened in Ouroboros.[42]
    • Even Harumi didn't know that and so she wanted revenge on the ninja for her parents' death, not on Pythor.[43]
  • When Pythor folds his hood at the end of "The Curse of the Golden Master," it is possible to see a stud on his black head for a short time before he shows up.[44]
  • Pythor's arc in Rebooted seams to be inspired by Saruman from The Lord of the Rings as they both were figures dressed in white helping the big evil while still having personal ambitions.
  • After being bleached by the Devourer, Pythor's voice sounded more deep and gravelly, almost like he is sick.
    • Nevertheless, this is only the case for "The Curse of the Golden Master," as in the next episode his voice returned to normal, even though it was a little higher.
    • Tommy Andreasen explained, "We had to camouflage his identity until the reveal. And the[n] back to good old Pythor."[45]
  • The Overlord would possibly have gotten rid of or betrayed Pythor eventually, as he did with Garmadon.[46]
  • In LEGO Ninjago: Shadow of Ronin, Pythor, in his non-bleached form, is the most expensive of the Serpentine, costing 500,000 studs, likely due to his popularity and importance.
  • In The Realm of Shadows, a shrunken Pythor is seen caged behind Wu.
    • According to the Hageman Brothers, Pythor was not in the script.[47]
  • Kai states in "Ninjago's Most Wanted" that Pythor only helped them defeat the Anacondrai Cultists because he knew the Anacondrai generals would make him big again. This would explain his easy descent back into villainy as of "Day of the Departed."
  • According to Misako, Pythor is as much cat as he is snake, as he has nine lives,[48] thus interfering with his perseverance in the constant attempt to conquer Ninjago and and seek revenge on the ninja.
  • Pythor appears in The LEGO Ninjago Movie Videogame as a boss in the training dojo "The Slithering Catacombs" and can be unlocked as a playable character by achieving gold medal status in the said dojo, which requires the player to accumulate at least 170,000 studs.
    • However, this is his white-scaled, and his purple-scaled self is not present in the game.
  • He was credited in "The Weekend Drill" despite not appearing in the episode.
  • Pythor appears in up to two sets on a ninja computer screen as a wanted person. These are 70596 Samurai X Cave Chaos and 71741 Ninjago City Gardens.
  • According to Tommy Andreasen, it's possible Pythor could become purple again by shedding his scales.[49]
  • According to Tommy Andreasen, Pythor and Aspheera would likely not get along well, as there would be "Too much ego on each side."[50]
    • This was later clarified in the episode, "The Council of the Crystal King," and served as a recurring element in subsequent episodes of Crystalized.
  • When asked for an update on Pythor's post-Merge status, Chris "Doc" Wyatt stated that he is "Happy, healthy, and leading an uneventful life."[2]
  • Pythor, SsssSsss Underwood and the Slitherbottom family are the only Serpentine to have last names and along with Alfonzo Frohicky, the only anthropomorphic animals to have surnames.

Relationships

These are the relationships of Pythor.

Allies

Allies[]

Arcturus[]

“Thank you, Pythor. You should be rewarded for your courage and bravery. You have made your ancestors proud. Finally.”
— Arcturus to Pythor, "The Corridor of Elders"

During the Serpentine War, Arcturus was Pythor's general. They often discussed the Anacondrai's plans together and despite only doing what was best for him, Pythor obeyed Arcturus and even praised and admired him for his deeds during the war.

Forty years after the war, when Garmadon sacrificed himself to win the Second Serpentine War and released the Anacondrai generals, Arcturus' spirit thanked Pythor for his help, praising his courage and bravery. He claimed his ancestors would be proud and even restored Pythor to his original size.

Strike[]

“Well, I must hand it to you, Strike, you were right after all... the Anacondrai did join in on the festivities. Now all the tribes are together in the happy family reunion you always dreamed of.”
— Pythor to Strike, Strike of the Serpentine

During the Serpentine War, Pythor was often with Strike discussing the conflict with humans. He mocked her plans to unite all the Serpentine tribes and the fact that only the war could do that. However, Strike trusted Pythor because she thought he was on her side, until Pythor finally revealed to her that he was only on his own side.

Skales (formerly)[]

“Skales, my long-lost friend, how good to see you.”
— Pythor to Skales, Pythor's Revenge

Skales was Pythor's second-in-command.

After Pythor released the Constrictai and Venomari, Skales came in contact with Pythor and helped him to bring the Serpentine tribes together. Skales assisted Pythor in his quest to obtain the Fangblades and unleash the Great Devourer, although he does express some concerns for the plan in the beginning, saying that Pythor was chasing children's stories. Nevertheless, Skales remained loyal to him for quite some time and often fought by his side, advised, or protected him against the ninja. This loyalty was short-lived however, as after Pythor's presumed death at the hands of the Devourer, Skales realized the depth of his actions and fled alongside his fellow Serpentine, hiding out in the Fangpyre Tomb.

Years later, Skales wasn't very happy to see Pythor's return a day after the Yin-Yang Eclipse thinking that he was connected to Anacondrai War. After Pythor's failed attempt to show the BorgWatch technology, Skales told him that his desperation has overstepped all boundaries and even made him look ridiculous.

The Overlord[]

“Haha! The people are losing hope. Soon they will bow to you, Golden Master.”
— Pythor to the Overlord, "The Titanium Ninja"

Pythor allied himself with The Overlord to get vengeance on the ninja for letting the Great Devourer eat him. The Overlord was shocked at Pythor restoring him, though he gained a liking for Pythor after he saw how vile and cunning he was and both worked to capture Lloyd.

During the Nindroid crisis, Pythor shielded the Overlord from the ninja's attack and ended up being shrunk.

Years later, Pythor joined the Crystal Council, a group working for the Overlord. Pythor was once again a loyal servant to his master, although he was nearly killed by the Overlord along with the other members of the council for not finding the ninja's hideout.

Cryptor[]

“Ah, Cryptor, my loyal friend.”
— Pythor to Cryptor, "Day of the Departed"

Cryptor was one of Pythor's allies. As Pythor was advisor to the Overlord and Cryptor was the general of the Overlord's nindroids, they were often seen together and worked well. However, this was not always the case because Cryptor did threaten Pythor if he lied about their master and Pythor intimidated him with the threat of reprogramming should he step out of line.

On the Day of the Departed Pythor happily greets his old friend after Cryptor's revival, showing no ill will towards him. In return, Cryptor didn't show much emotion to Pythor but wasn't hostile to him.

Aspheera[]

“The time for revenge is at hand. Revenge. Revenge!”
“Revenge, revenge.”
“What?”
“What what?”
“What did you say?”
“I don't know. What did I say?”
— Aspheera and Pythor, "The Council of the Crystal King"

Aspheera is a new ally of Pythor during the events of Crystalized, although the two didn't get along well.

During the council's meeting, when Aspheera announced the the time for revenge was near, Pythor mocked her by parroting her line "Revenge, Revenge." When Aspheera asked the Anacondrai what he had said, Pythor just played it dumb, further insulting her.

During the monastery siege, Aspheera started shouting for revenge, to which Pythor responded by shaking his head in annoyance.

While Aspheera was making the ritual to revive the Overlord, Pythor was mimicking her.


Enemies

Enemies[]

Wu[]

“Well, if they're impostors, you're cowards.”
“And what are you? There's a reason we never trust a snake.”
— Pythor and Wu, "The Greatest Fear of All"
This section is a stub. You can help expand this section by adding some information.


Garmadon[]

“I never thought I'd say this, but Pythor is right.”
— Garmadon, "The Corridor of Elders"
This section is a stub. You can help expand this section by adding some information.


Ninja (temporary allies)[]

“Help you? The ninja? You fed me to the Devourer, defeated every army I've aligned with, even forced me to swallow your shrinking pill! Haven't you done enough damage to my diminishing ego?”
— Pythor to the ninja, "The Greatest Fear of All"

The ninja are Pythor's archenemies. After being released from the tomb by Lloyd, Pythor and the boy were attacked by the ninja, who immediately began to hate each other. Over the following time, the ninja constantly tried to thwart Pythor's plans, which they always succeeded in, defeating every army he allied with. The only time Pythor was willing to help the ninja was during the Second Serpentine War, but only because of fear of Chen.

Lloyd[]

“Somehow, it's fitting that this would come down to you and me.”
— Pythor to Lloyd, "The Coming of the King"

Pythor manipulated Lloyd to get his hands on the map to the Serpentine tombs and wasted no time in betraying after his usefulness ran out.

Pythor later allied himself with the Overlord to get vengeance on Lloyd for letting the Great Devourer eat him but it resulted in him being shrunk and imprisoned in Kryptarium Prison.

During the Second Serpentine War, Pythor wasn't pleased to see Lloyd again but had no choice but to help the ninja. Lloyd even protected Pythor from Chen's forces who were coming to claim him. In the final battle, they met again and Pythor gave the ninja a spell that would banish Chen and his followers to the Cursed Realm. By doing this, Pythor became a temporary ally to the ninja, despite the spell banishing Lloyd's father, Garmadon too.

They do not see each other for several seasons but were mostly on neutral terms.

On the Day of the Departed, Pythor fell back into his evil ways and decided to use the events of the day to destroy Lloyd since he defeated his father. They fought and Pythor use underhanded moves such as holding Lloyd's mother hostage but Lloyd and his mother broke free and Pythor disappeared into the night.

Shortly before the Crystal Infection, Pythor met Lloyd again and tried to fight him.

Jay[]

“Ha! Take that, exalted Serpentine King, Pythor Chumsworth. That'll teach you not to mess with honesty, dependency, distributives, or fine foods!”
— Jay to Pythor, "Blue Lightning"

Jay and Pythor have not interacted much when the latter was released from his tomb, but they did oppose each other as Jay fought with his team against the Serpentine.

Sometime during these events, Jay halted Pythor and some Venomari soldiers in his heist of hijacking noodle trucks.

In "Once Bitten, Twice Shy," when a Serpentine-transformed Jay was trying to find Nya at Mega Monster Amusement Park, he found Pythor and the Serpentine and tried to engage in battle, but Pythor and the others mocked him for his tail, before sending Nya off on the rollercoaster.

During the Nindroid crisis, Jay and the others soon became aware that Pythor had resurfaced and led the Nindroids to bring the Overlord back into Ninjago.

Jay and the other ninja visited a miniaturized Pythor at Kryptarium for help on how to defeat Chen and his army that were transformed into Anacondrai.

Years later, during the final conflict, Jay and the other ninja unlocked their Dragon Forms and fought their respective members of the Crystal Council. Pythor was paired against Jay after the latter restrained him from attacking Kai. Jay used a Lightning quake to force Pythor to drop his invisibility and knocking him out, allowing Jay to take back his Nunchucks of Lightning from the former Serpentine King.

Chen[]

“What about me? You can't just leave me here! Where's the honor in that?”
“Oh, right, honor. Like you said, we aren't real Anacondrai. No, we are not. No, no, no.”
— Pythor and Chen, "The Greatest Fear of All"

Because of Chen and his followers turning themselves into Anacondrai, Pythor grew dislike at their audacity to masquerading as his proud race.

Pythor's disgust for them increased after he learned Chen caused the Serpentine War by lying to both sides. After Chen's warriors captured him, Pythor insulted them by calling them frauds, as they had him chased by a Swamp Rat to sweat out essence for them to maintain their form. Pythor was not pleased when a mocking Chen left him to his fate of nearly being devoured by a swamp rat.

As revenge, Pythor tamed the rat and gave the ninja a spell that could defeat the impostors. He watched gleefully as they were banished to the Cursed Realm.

During "Day of the Departed," Chen and Pythor met again with neither being pleased to see the other and giving a tense acknowledgment. Despite that, they were united in wanting vengeance on the ninja.

New Ninja[]

“Yes, I got busted. By the New Ninja, who are so much better than you ever were, by the way.”
— Pythor to the ninja, "Kryptarium Prison Blues"

Although they did not meet many times, the New Ninja were the ones who arrested Pythor and placed him in Kryptarium Prison after the Great Flood. Nevertheless, Pythor praised them before the ninja and said that they were much better, although it was mainly intended to provoke the original ninja and probably did not express his true view of the New Ninja.

Skylor[]

“Skylor? You’re the one with the ability to-”
“Yep.”
“Impressive. But even your powers will be negated by my vengestone soldiers.”
— Pythor and Skylor, "Safe Haven"

In "Safe Haven," when Pythor attempted to attack Kai and Cole, Skylor appeared, whom Pythor recognized and realized that she had the ability to absorb Elemental Powers. As Pythor was horrified by this realization, Skylor absorbed Kai's Fire and Cole's Earth and blasted them together at Pythor, who tried to cover them with nunchucks. The Anacondrai then admitted that it was impressive, but that even her powers would not hold up against his Vengestone soldiers. Skylor, however, used the power of Earth to raise a stone wall in the alley.
